brief.name: Fixture opera house with sails (invented)
brief.subject: fixture opera house with white sails on a podium

style.vernacular: Coastal capital on the Gulf of Guinea: colonial-era forts and Victorian-colonial buildings in Jamestown and Osu, low-rise painted-render and concrete houses and shops with corrugated roofs, mid-century modernist public buildings (1957-66), and glass-and-concrete towers and malls in Airport City and the Ridge area, on dusty red-brown ground with palms and neem-type trees.
style.ornament: Adinkra symbols and the Black Star of Ghana on monuments and gates (Akofena sword, Sankofa), kente-inspired colour bands in red, gold and green, mid-century concrete screens and sawtooth windows, colonial whitewashed fort walls with cannons.

sources.what: Colonial neighbourhoods (Osu/Christiansborg, Jamestown, Adabraka), forts, modern skyscrapers, Holy Trinity Cathedral, National Mosque, National Theatre, Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum, tropical savanna climate
1957 concrete museum by Denys Lasdun with saw-toothed windows and saucer dome, evidence of mid-century modernism
